text:
maria: heads-up — ran some examples for the ingest priority heuristic RFC and wanted to share concrete rule sets that we can land quickly.
chris: nice, short summary?
maria: goal: keep high-value traces+errors through during backpressure, degrade low-value verbose spans first, and preserve billing tags. tradeoffs: complexity vs cost savings.
devon: +1. do you have sample configs we can test in staging?
maria: yes — sketch below (pseudo-yaml):
```
priority_rules:
  - match: \"error || span.attr.critical == true\"
    action: keep
  - match: \"sampled == false && span.duration < 5ms && service == \\\"frontend-debug\\\"\"
    action: delay_or_drop
    max_delay_ms: 2000
  - match: \"metric.type == counter && rate > 1000/s\"
    action: aggregate_and_drop_raw
```
chris: so three classes: always-keep, delay/drop for low-value spans, and aggregate for high-cardinality noisy metrics.
samir: what about preserving cost attribution keys if we drop? we can't lose billing context otherwise usage reporting breaks.
maria: important question — plan is to always copy minimal billing keys (billing_project, team_id) into an envelope-level header before any drop. that header is tiny and cheap.
devon: envelope-level header sounds right. can we include an opt-out for customers who want zero extra metadata?
maria: yes, feature flag per-tenant in Dedicated/Private. Default: on for hosted.
chris: performance impact of copying headers? microbenchmarks?
maria: measured ~0.04us per envelope on p99 under load — negligible. main cost is added storage in logs if we keep full traces.
samir: how do we handle sampling for pre-enrich vs post-enrich? if we sample early, enrichment that adds billing keys might not run.
maria: rule: attach billing header as early as possible (edge proxy) before sampling decisions. if edge can't, then we fall back to heuristic lookup service (fast cache) — degrade accuracy a tiny bit.
devon: curious about the delay_or_drop action — how do we surface that to downstream consumers? e.g., traces that are delayed might skew latency observability.
maria: good point. plan: delayed spans get a synthetic_span.stall_reason = \"ingest_backpressure_delay\" and we emit a lightweight metric about the number of delayed spans so dashboards can account for it.
chris: need an explainer in the RFC that shows example dashboards and a migration checklist for SRE teams.
maria: will add. also proposing a short-lived ingestion token that marks preserved billing keys; useful for audits.
samir: any thoughts on backpressure thresholds? static vs adaptive?
maria: prefer adaptive based on queue depth + processing latency + admitted throughput. static thresholds cause oscillation.
devon: can we simulate with production trace replay? I can spin up a job to run our traces through the new rules and report: keep/delay/drop rates per service.
maria: yes please — can you run for 48h window and include edge-case services like mobile-sync and ingester-debug?
devon: will do.
chris: next steps: 1) maria adds config examples + dashboard sketches to RFC follow-up doc, 2) devon runs replay and posts numbers, 3) samir prototypes envelope-header copy in edge proxy. aim for staging rollout in two weeks.
maria: thanks — I'll create the follow-up doc and ping ops for a canary. :thumbsup:
ingest-bot: deploy-check — canary cluster has 12/12 healthy nodes for today.
chris: thanks everyone — filing a tiny follow-up ticket to track the header opt-out flag.
